papers.title: Optimal Mixing for Local Edge-Coloring Dynamics on Trees
papers.abstract: We study the mixing time of two local Markov chains for uniformly sampling proper edge colorings of trees. For a tree with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$, we establish optimal mixing-time bounds for the single-edge Glauber dynamics when $q\ge\Delta+2$ and for the neighboring-edge heat-bath dynamics when $q\ge\Delta+1$. Both chains mix in $O_\Delta(n(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ steps, uniformly over the number of colors $q$. These bounds are tight in their dependence on $n$ for fixed $\Delta$. Our proof establishes log-Sobolev inequalities through local color release, reusable recoloring buffers, and component entropy mixing. The two dynamics require different local constructions: a two-spare-color buffer for single-edge updates and a second-layer controller for neighboring-edge updates. The resulting entropy analysis applies to general bounded-degree trees, including regimes where worst-case spatial mixing fails.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for the Entropic Central Limit Theorem in the Log-Concave Case
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave isotropic probability measure on $R^d$ , and let $\mu^n$ denote the law of the normalized sum of $n$ independent random vectors with law $\mu$. We prove that \[ H(\mu^n|\gamma)\leq \frac{C}{n} \min\left\{1+\log(ed)^2H(\mu|\gamma)\ ,\ d\right\}. \] Compared to the previous best known bound, our estimate replaces the polynomial dependence on the dimension by a polylogarithmic one. The proof relies on a new combination of the De Bruijn identity with Eldan's stochastic localization process.

papers.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
papers.abstract: We study $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel.We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.

papers.title: A local-to-global principle for $f$-divergence homogenization
papers.abstract: We study the effect of replacing a family of independent statistical experiments by independent repetitions of their average. We give a simple, complete characterization of the $f$-divergences for which this operation increases divergence by at most a constant depending only on the generator, uniformly in the number of observations and the underlying measurable space. The characterization is governed by a local-to-global principle: a comparison restricted to two observations on a binary alphabet already determines the validity of the general inequality. It admits an explicit scalar formulation, which simplifies further for symmetric divergences. The result applies to arbitrary convex generators and requires no differentiability or symmetry assumptions. It recovers the homogenization inequality for total variation and identifies exactly the admissible members of the power-divergence family. In particular, whenever uniform homogenization fails, the obstruction is already present in a family of binary experiments with two observations. Moreover, the global comparison constant is controlled uniformly over generators with a common bound in the local inequality.

papers.title: Dimension-free regimes for unadjusted Langevin in ridge-separable models: A subspace robust Wasserstein analysis
papers.abstract: The Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (ULA) is widely used for high-dimensional Bayesian inference. Classical analyses in Wasserstein-2 distance predict an asymptotic bias and a mixing time that grow with dimension, but this metric is stronger than necessary for many statistical tasks. We instead analyze the bias in subspace robust Wasserstein distance, which controls the mean and arbitrary low-dimensional marginals and is therefore well suited to observables typically estimated in practice. For ridge-separable potentials formed with i.i.d. data, we prove high-probability bounds showing a bell-shaped mixing profile as the number of data points $N$ varies relative to the dimension $d$. In the overparameterized regime, the effective dimension is the rank $N$ of the data-dependent perturbation, leading to complexity depending on $N$ rather than $d$. In the large-sample regime, Gaussian-perturbation estimates yield dimension-free complexity once $N$ is sufficiently large. In contrast, near the proportional regime $\asymp d$, we prove that dimension-free guarantees are impossible in general.

papers.title: High-dimensional learning dynamics of multi-pass Stochastic Gradient Descent in multi-index models
papers.abstract: The learning dynamics of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) are believed to play an important role in influencing the generalization properties of trained models. While the precise dynamics of how online (one-pass) SGD optimizes the population risk are now understood in a broad range of high-dimensional problems, a comparable understanding of multi-pass SGD for empirical risk minimization is still largely lacking. In this work, we develop an asymptotically exact characterization of the dynamics of multi-pass SGD for a non-convex multi-index model, in the high-dimensional regime where sample size $n$ and data dimension $d$ increase proportionally. We consider any sub-linear batch size $\kappa \asymp n^\alpha$ with $\alpha \in [0,1)$ and a commensurate ``critical'' scaling of the learning rate, and show that the coordinate-wise dynamics of SGD admit a novel continuous-time scaling limit, given by a system of dynamical mean-field equations that are driven by a scalar Poisson jump process representing the asymptotic limit of SGD sampling noise. This scaling limit connects several previously disparate theories around SGD, namely (i) the classical interpretation of SGD as an approximation to gradient flow on the empirical risk, (ii) the characterization of online SGD via an autonomous ODE in its overlap statistics, and (iii) the coincidence between multi-pass SGD dynamics and diffusion approximations in least-squares problems. We illustrate how these perspectives are recovered by specializing our result to small learning rates, large sample sizes, and linear models, respectively. Outside of these specializations, the scaling limit of SGD is distinct both from diffusion approximations and gradient flow, and may enable SGD to converge to local optima of the non-convex empirical risk with different statistical properties.

papers.title: Central limit theorem in R\'enyi divergence for lattice random variables
papers.abstract: Let $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^n$ be independent, identically distributed lattice random variables with zero mean, unit variance, and maximal span $h>0$. Let $S_n=(X_1+\cdots+X_n)/\sqrt n$. Let $Z_n$ denote the quantization of a standard Gaussian random variable on the support lattice of $S_n$. We show that the R\'enyi divergence $D_\alpha(S_n\|Z_n)$ of order $1<\alpha<\infty$ tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if $D_\alpha(S_{n_0}\| Z_{n_0})<\infty$ for some integer $n_0$ and a sub-Gaussian condition holds. Furthermore, we derive an Edgeworth-type asymptotic expansion of the divergence to arbitrary order. We also show that the R\'enyi divergence $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)$ of infinite order tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if a sub-Gaussian condition, a curvature condition, and a uniform separation condition hold. These results constitute lattice counterparts of R\'enyi entropic central limit theorems for continuous random variables obtained by Bobkov, Chistyakov and G\"{o}tze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{47} (2019), 270--323) and Bobkov and G\"{o}tze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{53} (2025), 453--477). Uniform separation is an additional assumption beyond the sub-Gaussian and curvature conditions used in the continuous setting. The failure of uniform separation may cause an exponentially tilted version of $X_1$ to concentrate on a sublattice of max span $kh$ for some integer $k>1$, which yields the lower bound $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)\ge\log k$, and hence a failure of the entropic central limit theorem.

papers.title: Sparse power spectrum for passive scalars under Pierrehumbert flow
papers.abstract: We study the long-time Fourier distribution of driven passive scalars transported by an incompressible alternating shear flow (the Pierrehumbert flow) subjected to IID random phase shifts, in the regime of strong shear-strength. With a novel and self-contained proof, we establish (i) a quantitative version of the cumulative Batchelor's law; (ii) quantitative negative regularity mixing estimates; and (iii) a strong form of `sparsity' -- unevenness in the distribution of Fourier mass in radial sectors in frequency space. Our method uses the strong shear-strength assumption to handle a purely deterministic scalar driving term.

papers.title: Radial $\Phi^4$ models in supercritical regimes
papers.abstract: We consider the $\Phi^4_d$ measure under radial symmetry on the unit ball, formally given by $$d\rho(u) = \frac 1 Z \exp\Big( - \frac 14 \int_{B_1} |u|^4 dx - \frac 12 \int_{B_1} |\nabla u|^2 dx\Big) d u, $$ where $u$ is restricted to radially symmetric functions with 0 boundary conditions. We prove that for every dimension $d$, there exists such a measure, which is concentrated on $L^p(B_1)$ for every $p < \frac{2d}{d-2}$ (for every $p < \infty$ if $d \le 2$). Furthermore, we show that these measures are not Gaussian, and when $d \ge 4$, they are singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We achieve this result by first defining the measure $\rho^+_\delta[\lambda]$ on the shell $\{\delta \le |x| \le 1\}$, $0 < \delta < 1$, with a boundary condition on the sphere of radius $\delta$ of the form $u|_{\{|x| = \delta\}} = \lambda$. Then we prove that this measure satisfies a variational formula, and use it to show moment bounds which are uniform in the boundary value $\lambda$. A crucial ingredient in this argument is the fact that every solution of the elliptic equation $-\Delta u + u^3 = 0$ on the annulus $\{ \delta \le |x| \le 1 \}$ satisfies uniform bounds inside the domain, independently of the boundary conditions.

papers.title: A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs
papers.abstract: We provide a general ansatz for the paracontrolled approach introduced by Gubinelli, Imkeller, Perkowski for treating singular SPDEs. The ansatz proposed covers a large class of equations. It is described via decorated trees that encode its coefficients and its stochastic data. The main novelty is the recursive definition of the paracontrolled stochastic iterated integrals that involve a well-chosen combinatorial set of words. The paralinearisation is performed via a lift of iterated paraproducts to modelled distributions. The main idea is to integrate localised iterated paraproducts in order to get a global object with a good regularity. We also provide a fixed point argument and the renormalised equation with this ansatz when one uses the preparation map formalism that encompasses the BPHZ renormalisation. The last main result is the convergence of the renormalised stochastic data via the BPHZ renormalisation using an adaptation of the spectral gap approach. One obtains in the end a general solution theory for parabolic singular SPDEs via the paracontrolled approach.

papers.title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
papers.abstract: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.

papers.title: On Arithmetic-Progression Biases in Random Partitions: Limiting Laws and the Li-Zhao Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $\cR=\{r+jm:j\geq0\}$ and $\cS=\{s+jm:j\geq0\}$ be disjoint arithmetic progressions of positive integers, and choose a partition of $n$ uniformly at random. We determine the limiting probability that the number of parts in $\cR$ is larger than the number of parts in $\cS$. More precisely, if $a=r/m$ and $b=s/m$, then this probability converges to $I_{1/2}(a,b)$, the regularized incomplete beta function. We prove the stronger distributional statement that, after multiplication by the partition saddle-point parameter, the difference of the two numbers of parts converges to $m^{-1}(\log G_b-\log G_a)$, where $G_a$ and $G_b$ are independent gamma variables. The proof uses the Boltzmann conditioning device for random partitions, a $q$-gamma evaluation of the unconditioned characteristic function, and a uniform Fourier estimate showing that conditioning on the total size does not change the limit. We also evaluate the finite-truncation limit studied by Li and Zhao. The two evaluations coincide, proving their conjecture on the commutation of the truncation and large-size limits.

papers.title: Random Survivor Sets with Moving Holes in Bedford-McMullen Carpets
papers.abstract: Let $2\le m < n$ be integers, and let $K(\mathcal{A})$ be the Bedford--McMullen carpet generated by $\{(x,y)\mapsto((x+i)/m,(y+j)/n):(i,j)\in\mathcal{A}\}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is a subset of $\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\times\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $\mathcal{B}$ for the set of occupied columns, and assume that $\#\mathcal{B}\ge2$ and each column contains at least two symbols of $\mathcal{A}$. At each vertex of the column tree $\mathcal{B}^*$, we independently choose one forbidden symbol from $\mathcal{A}$ according to a prescribed distribution. Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the resulting product measure on $\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. This gives a random survivor set $K_\omega(\mathcal{A})$ with $\omega\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. We show that, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega$, \begin{equation*} \dim_H K_\omega(\mathcal{A})=\frac{1}{\log m}\log\left(\int \sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\ell_b(\omega)^{\frac{\log m}{\log n}} d\mathbb{P}(\omega)\right), \end{equation*} where $\ell_b(\omega)$ is the number of surviving symbols in column $b$ at the root.

papers.title: Combinatorial formulas for the multivariate Markov-Krein transform
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the Markov--Krein correspondence in both the univariate and multivariate settings. Our main result provides an explicit moment--moment formula expressing the multivariate moments of the inverse Markov--Krein transform in terms of the multivariate moments of the Markov-Krein transform via cyclic interval partitions. We also derive moment--cumulant relations involving classical, Boolean and free cumulants.

papers.title: Optimal CLT error bounds in the second order Wasserstein metric via Stein's method for weakly dependent sequences
papers.abstract: We use Stein's method to prove general upper bounds on the second order Wasserstein distance in the CLT for general dependent partial sums $S_N=X_1+\ldots +X_N$. Then we use these estimates to provide optimal $O(N^{-1/2})$ rates for a variety of chaotic dynamical systems and $\phi$- and $\psi$-mixing sequences. Our results for $\psi$-mixing sequences are obtained under the fourth moment condition, which matches the best known results in the iid case. This is the first time that optimal CLT rates of any kind are obtained for unbounded weakly stationary variables under general mixing conditions. We then apply this result and obtain optimal CLT rates $O\left((\text{Var}(S_N))^{-1/2}\right)$ for non-stationary $\psi$-mixing sequences without any growth rates on $\text{Var}(S_N)$. We also obtain close to optimal CLT rates for nonconventional sums and some classes of random dynamical systems with non-uniform decay of correlations

papers.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
papers.abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $\theta_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge \theta_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $\theta_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^\beta$, for any given $\beta\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $\theta_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.

papers.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
papers.abstract: For a $\Delta$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{\Delta/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $\Delta \geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In contrast, for $\Delta=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to be different. Moreover, conditioned on the upper tail event of cycle counts in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, we show that the random graph contains a disjoint collection of clique and biclique like structures with probability approaching to one, a stark contrast compared to the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In the complementary regime, i.e.~for $1 \ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H} \ll (\log n)^{\alpha^*_H/(\alpha^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges in $H$, $\alpha^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including the regular case), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all of the unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.

papers.title: Geometry of Unimodular Random Hyperbolic Polyhedra
papers.abstract: We develop a geometric and probabilistic theory of unimodular random infinite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$, allowing ordinary, ideal, and hyperideal vertices. Our results relate local dihedral geometry to global conformal type and random-walk behavior. A central role is played by a geometric characteristic $L_f(P)$, determined by the dihedral angles incident to a face $f$. We establish the unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity $$ \mathbb E[L_f(P)]=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\mathbb E[deg(f)]. $$ Together with circle-pattern uniformization, this yields a sharp parabolic-hyperbolic dichotomy governed by the expected geometric characteristic. We also introduce polyhedral soficity and prove that admissible Benjamini-Schramm limits of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra are parabolic. We further establish a quantitative Ring Lemma for regular circle patterns, providing degree-sensitive geometric control without assuming bounded degrees. Combined with unimodular probability methods, this estimate enables us to identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Our results extend the geometric-characteristic theory beyond ideal polyhedra, connecting three-dimensional geometry, unimodular Gauss-Bonnet theory, and stochastic boundary behavior.

papers.title: Atomic limits of empirical measures of interacting particle systems with self-duality
papers.abstract: We study the fixed-particle limit of empirical measures for a unified self-dual family of conservative particle systems on $\mathbb{Z}^d$: independent random walkers, the symmetric exclusion process, and the symmetric inclusion process. For a fixed number of particles $k$, under diffusive space-time scaling parametrised by $n$, we prove that as $n\to\infty$ the normalised empirical measure converges in $D([0,T],\mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R}^d))$ to an atomic empirical measure carried by $k$ independent diffusions, with constant covariance determined by the microscopic jump kernel. Equivalently, the limit is the unique atomic solution of the Dean-Kawasaki martingale problem with mass quantisation $1/k$. In particular, exclusion and inclusion have the same fixed-$k$ atomic limit as independent walkers: the interaction contributes only through microscopic near-collisions, whose rescaled occupation time vanishes. The proof combines self-duality, consistency-based reduction to two particles, and Green-function estimates for finite perturbations of symmetric random walks.

papers.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
papers.abstract: This work constructs a non-trivial solution to the ill-defined two-dimensional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation at criticality: a distribution-valued stochastic process on the plane, which we call the Critical 2D KPZ Process. It arises as the limit in law of centred log partition functions of two-dimensional Gaussian directed polymers at criticality, viewed as discretised KPZ solutions. It is also a measurable function of the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) via a renormalised Cole-Hopf transformation, obtained as the limit of the centred logarithm of the spatially mollified SHF as the smoothing is removed. The Critical 2D KPZ process is non-Gaussian and its covariance displays a log-log blow-up near the diagonal. Gaussian fluctuations emerge when averaging on shrinking spatial scales. The results presented here were obtained through extensive interactions with generative AI (ChatGPT 5.5, 5.6 and 6); see Appendix C for more details. The proof builds on key recent and older advances in our field, combined in novel ways with substantial AI input. We view this manuscript as a "community project" that represents more than a decade's collective effort. We have worked on making the presentation as accessible as possible, highlighting the main ideas and their relations to the literature.

papers.title: On the direct SLE-martingale approach to the integrability of Conformal Loop Ensembles
papers.abstract: This paper is about the derivation of "integrability results" (i.e., for example, explicit formulas for the probability of events involving a few marked points) for Conformal Loop Ensembles, that are the (conjectured) scaling limits of discrete crititical planar lattice models from Statistical Physics. We discuss the explicit solutions to the PDEs provided by the original SLE/CLE martingale approach that AI now makes it possible to uncover. This provides short and direct new proofs of a number of formulas that have recently been derived based on Liouville quantum gravity, conformal field theory or Coulomb gas methods, and also makes it possible to derive some new ones. We briefly illustrate this with the examples of the backbone exponent and annulus crossing probabilities for critical percolation, but this direct approach seems to apply to a wide class of observables of two-dimensional systems related to conformal field theories.

papers.title: Sampling from Spherical Spin Glasses in Total Variation via Algorithmic Stochastic Localization
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of algorithmically sampling from the Gibbs measure of a mixed $p$-spin spherical spin glass. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that samples from the Gibbs measure up to vanishing total variation error, for any model whose mixture satisfies $$ \xi''(s) < \frac{1}{(1-s)^2}, \qquad \forall s\in [0,1). $$ Our algorithm follows the algorithmic stochastic localization (SL) approach introduced in (Alaoui, Montanari, Sellke, 2022) and in fact achieves a more difficult task. Namely, it (approximately) generates a sample path $({\boldsymbol y}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ from the SL process. For large $T$, ${\boldsymbol y}_T/T$ is an approximate sample from the target Gibbs measure, and hence we solve the original problem as a special case. We provide evidence that the condition $\xi''(s) < (1-s)^{-2}$ is sharp for the task of sampling SL sample paths. Furthermore, we prove that it is optimal within a class of generalized SL processes. Remarkably this threshold is close to the conjectured threshold for sampling from the original Gibbs measure. In particular, for the pure $p$-spin glasses it is within an absolute ($p$-independent) constant of the so-called shattering phase transition. Earlier work on related models was suboptimal by a factor diverging polynomially in $p$. A key step of this approach is to estimate the mean of a sequence of tilted measures. We produce an improved estimator for this task by identifying a suitable correction to the TAP fixed point selected by approximate message passing (AMP). As a consequence, we improve the algorithm's guarantee over previous work, from normalized Wasserstein to total variation error. In particular, the new algorithm and analysis open the way to perform inference about one-dimensional projections of the measure.

papers.title: Moments Comparison Inequalities for Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow, Polymers and GMC
papers.abstract: We employ a Gaussian convex inequality developed in [AC15], [Che26], [Gue22], and [FUMPC26] to establish (one sided) moment comparison inequalities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos, directed polymers in Gaussian environment and, in particular, the Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF), including upper bounds on negative moments, as well as similar lower bounds for $p$-th moments with $p\in (0,1)$. For the Critical 2d SHF, averaged over small balls, we also obtain the matching (up to multiplicative constants) complementary bounds. We establish the complementary bounds using a bootstrap argument inspired by [DS10] and a geometric decomposition introduced in [GT26]. Specifically, we prove that for locally averaged SHF, for every $p\in\mathbb R$, the $p$-th moment is, up to multiplicative constants, bounded in both sides by the $\frac{p(p-1)}{2}$-th power of its second moment.

papers.title: Relaxation and Steady-State Entropy Production for Langevin SPDEs: A Dirichlet-Form Approach
papers.abstract: We develop a Dirichlet-form framework for relaxation and steady-state entropy production in preconditioned Langevin stochastic partial differential equations. In infinite dimensions, the usual Fokker--Planck calculations based on ambient Lebesgue densities and the corresponding probability-current densities are generally unavailable. For the detailed-balance class, a quasi-regular symmetric Dirichlet form on the Gibbs state space yields an exact de Bruijn entropy-dissipation formula for regular densities and an integrated inequality for arbitrary finite-entropy initial laws. Self-adjointness gives detailed balance and stationary path reversal, while a coordinate-martingale criterion identifies the associated process with the prescribed SPDE. For the one-dimensional $\Phi^4_1$ and convex Allen--Cahn-type Gibbs dynamics, we combine the established strong well-posedness theory with direct verification of the logarithmic derivatives, form closure, quasi-regularity and form--SPDE correspondence, and obtain relative-entropy decay bounds with exponents $2$ and $2(1-\lambda/m)$, respectively, with $m>\lambda$ in the latter case. Away from detailed balance, bounded skew-adjoint linear forcing preserves a Gaussian invariant law without requiring commutation between the forcing and covariance. We identify the antisymmetric action on cylinder observables and its Cameron--Martin current and prove that the squared current energy equals the steady-state entropy-production rate defined by forward--reverse path-space relative entropy per unit time, as well as the monotone limit of the Galerkin rates. Under commutation, we additionally obtain an explicit transient Onsager decomposition after a mass quench. Exclusion processes and Gaussian rotors provide finite-state and Gaussian benchmarks.

papers.title: Strong freezing in binary perceptron models
papers.abstract: The binary perceptron model concerns the set of solutions obtained by intersecting random half-spaces. One of the most striking physics predictions for this model, going back to Krauth and M\'ezard [KM89] and sharpened in [HWK13, HK14], is strong freezing: typical solutions are at Hamming distance of order $n$ from every other solution. This phenomenon has attracted a lot of attention over the years, partly because of its intricate connections to statistical physics and computational complexity. We prove strong freezing at every positive constraint density for a general class of perceptron models and for any disorder with independent entries of mean zero and unit variance. More precisely, with probability at least $1-e^{-c\sqrt n}$, all but an $e^{-c\sqrt n}$ fraction of the solutions have no other solution within Hamming distance $\delta n$. In particular, our result includes the asymmetric binary perceptron at every margin, for which strong freezing has been a long-standing open problem [KM89,HWK13,HK14], and the symmetric binary perceptron, for which we recover the strong freezing results of Perkins and Xu [PX24] and of Abbe, Li and Sly [ALS21]. Our proof crucially relies on replacing the number of constraints by a Poisson variable, which makes the numbers of constraints cutting out different subsets of the hypercube independent. Since each constraint can only remove solutions, the FKG inequality then decouples the partition function from the event that two nearby configurations are both solutions.

papers.title: Exponential decay of fractional moments in the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$
papers.abstract: For the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$, we show that, at energy zero, the fractional moments of Green functions, $\mathbb E[ G(x,y)^s]$ decay exponentially in the distance between $x$ and $y$, for every constant edge weight $W>0$ and every $0<s<1/2$. Here $ G$ is the infinite-volume Green function of the associated random Schr\"odinger operator. The main ingredient is a quantitative lower bound on the derivative of the mean effective conductance with respect to the edge weights.

papers.title: Advance versus Spot Selling in Queueing Systems: the Effect of Uncertainty Sources
papers.abstract: We develop an unobservable M/M/1 queueing model to analyze advance selling and spot selling under uncertainty. Customers are heterogeneous in waiting costs, drawn from a uniform distribution. We disentangle two fundamental sources of uncertainty: customer valuation and service capacity. We derive the respective revenue functions for both advance and spot selling strategies and compare their performance. Our analysis reveals that advance selling is more profitable when customer valuations are uncertain. Conversely, spot selling emerges as the more profitable strategy when uncertainty originates from service capacity. When both sources are present, our numerical experiments suggest that the preferred regime depends on the relative dispersion of the two uncertainties: advance selling tends to be favored when valuation uncertainty is sufficiently pronounced relative to capacity uncertainty, whereas spot selling tends to be favored when capacity uncertainty is more pronounced. These results highlight how the origin and magnitude of uncertainty shape the optimal selling strategy in service queues and offer practical guidance for platforms and service providers deciding between advance and spot selling.

papers.title: Ergodic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Stochastic Coefficients
papers.abstract: We investigate ergodic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with stochastic coefficients and introduce the associated stochastic ergodic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, in which the classical ergodic constant is replaced by a random process $\lambda$. We establish well-posedness of the equation and show that $\lambda$ characterizes the optimal ergodic costs for a general class of averaging kernels, including those corresponding to normalized finite-horizon and discounted costs. For random-periodic coefficients, we construct a random-periodic solution and show that the optimal ergodic costs associated with all admissible averaging kernels coincide. We also establish stability of the optimal ergodic costs under perturbations of the coefficients.

papers.title: Generalized Images for Brownian First Passage to Monomial Boundaries
papers.abstract: We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.

papers.title: A note on functional non-central limit theorem for periodic regime-switching stable-like processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a functional non-central limit theorem for regime-switching stable-like processes with periodic coefficients. Our approach relies on stochastic analysis methods, in particular semimartingale characteristics, combined with the ergodic theory of Markov processes. If the set on which the order function achieves its minimum value $\underline{\alpha}$ has positive Lebesgue measure, then the limit is a rotationally invariant $\underline{\alpha}$-stable L\'evy process. Otherwise, the limit is the zero process.
